For each of the following scenarios,
determine the appropriate method of analysis:

a. A $\chi^2$ test;
b. A paired $t$-test for the mean difference;
c. A two-sample $t$-test
d. None of the above.

If 'None of the above' is chosen,
can you identify the correct analysis?


1. Populations of the scaled quail have been decreasing.
  An observational research study [@data:pleasant:quail] examined the nests of scaled quails 
  to determine some of the reasons for this decline. 
  In each nest, the researchers recorded the maximum temperature during the first 21 days posthatch.  

  Two groups of nests were compared: 
  when the hen was present at 21 days posthatch ($n = 17$ nests), 
  and when the hen was absent at 21 days posthatch ($n = 37$ nests).   
  
  The aim was to see if the average maximum temperature was different for both groups (hen present; hen absent).  
  What is the appropriate method of analysis?

2. Many studies have observed an association between the presence of airborne allergens 
   and people reporting asthma. 
   To better understand the risks of airborne allergens, a study [@data:Targonski:mold] 
   examined the records for numerous people who died of asthma.  
   
   For each person, 
   they recorded the race of each person, 
   and whether the season when they died was pollen or non-pollen season.  
   
   The aim was to see if a relationship was present between the season (pollen or non-pollen) 
   and the race of the person.  
   
   What is the appropriate method of analysis?

3. An experimental study [@data:VanLeit2002:ChildrenWithDisabilities]
   "evaluated the impact of an 8-week psychosocial occupational therapy intervention program for mothers
   who have children with disabilities" (p. 402).

   Each mother was evaluated on their satisfaction in how they are spending their time,
   using the (quantitative) TUA scale.
   Mothers have their TUA score measured before and after the intervention to see
   if the intervention made a difference to TUA scores.

   What is the appropriate method of analysis?

4. A experimental study [@data:Ingenbleek2012:Vegetarianism] compared vegetarians to non-vegetarians on many criteria,
   to "explain why vegetarian subjects develop morbidity and mortality from cardiovascular diseases
   unrelated to vitamin&nbsp;B status and Framingham criteria".

   In one example,
   each person in the study was described as vegetarian or not,
   and each person's serum lipids (in mmol/L) was assessed.

   What is the appropriate method of analysis?

5. A study 
   compared the relationship between the VO2 max
   (a measure of an individual of an individual physical fitness) and 3km running velocity,
   for a set of male long-distance runners.

   What is the appropriate method of analysis?
